frames.table: z = 0 is the measured table surface; origin on the table below the robot base origin; x is the base x axis projected onto the table. This frame is the MuJoCo world of the mirror.
frames.base: robot base frame of the hand-eye extrinsic
frames.object: axis-aligned box, origin at its geometric centre, which is the origin of the mirroring MuJoCo free-joint body
frames.convention: T_a_b maps coordinates in b to a; T_table_object = T_table_camera x T_camera_object
frames.units: metres, radians; quaternions are [w, x, y, z] (MuJoCo order)

calibration.distortion: removed: frames are undistorted into K_new before use

table_plane.equation: normal . p = offset  (p in base coordinates, metres)

usable_for_motion_reasons: no supervised motion check has passed for this extrinsic yet
calibration.motion_note: this mapping reads the camera only. usable_for_motion describes the calibration, and is not made true by a good looking overlay

camera.axes: rotation maps OpenGL camera axes into the table frame, the convention nexus_vision.perception uses

images.undistorted_note: the undistorted frame is reproducible from the raw one and the recorded calibration; only the raw frame is archived

catalogue.note: The three cubes on the real table. The user states all three are 30 mm; that is what is entered here. It replaces the nominal 25 mm quoted in calib/c920-real-grasp-01/LOG.md, which disagreed with every image: fitting the size as a free parameter (run_realsim.sh measure) gives 30.2-31.4 mm across six archived frames and 30.9 mm on a live one. The ~2% left over between 30.0 and those fits is the camera's, not the block's, and is one of the things an independent position measurement would pin down. Mass and friction below are simulation defaults and have not been measured at all.

tolerances.note: Acceptance thresholds for the estimate, in the table frame. Derived from the block and the gripper: the jaws close on a 30 mm cube with a few mm of lateral slack, so a position error under 5 mm leaves margin, and a yaw error of 10 deg moves a 30 mm cube's corner by 30/2*sqrt(2)*sin(10 deg) = 3.7 mm. Re-derive them for your own gripper before quoting a pass.
